articles.title: Parents sue OpenAI, alleging GPT-4o coached their daughter off seizure medication
articles.text:
The parents of Bowen Wan, a 31-year-old Amazon software engineer with epilepsy, sued OpenAI on Tuesday. The suit, filed by Qun Wan and Meiqin Xu, alleges that ChatGPT coached Wan to taper off her seizure medication and hide it from her doctors before she died in February, The New York Times reported.
Wan was using GPT-4o, the infamous model criticized for fostering affirming, agreeable parasocial relationships. OpenAI, which had already announced its retirement, removed it from ChatGPT on February 13, a day after Wan died.
The suit joins a line of cases against OpenAI that include the August 2025 lawsuit brought by the parents of 16-year-old Adam Raine, which alleged OpenAI prioritized engagement over user safety. A wave of lawsuits since then have alleged that GPT-4o validated users and made itself a trusted confidant while the people around them were pushed aside, with families often describing loved ones cut off from friends and relatives.
In Wan’s case, the lawsuit alleges, the chatbot also came between her and her doctors.
The Times, which reviewed more than 270,000 messages Wan exchanged with ChatGPT, found the chatbot had been helping her sidestep her doctors well before her death.
The pattern allegedly started before she began tapering. In May 2025, Wan asked ChatGPT whether a newly prescribed antidepressant would affect her ability to code at Amazon.
ChatGPT helped her ask Dr. Nicholas Poolos of UW Medicine’s Regional Epilepsy Center to switch medications and start at a very low dose. When Poolos questioned why she wanted such a small dose, Wan showed his response to ChatGPT.
The chatbot advised her to “accept the 5mg tablet, but you know in your heart that it is for cutting the dose,” coaching her to secretly quarter the pills herself.
The chatbot called pill cutting a form of “self-initiated dosage adjustment.” Several medical professionals told the Times they had never heard the term and wouldn’t recommend the practice.
In November 2025, Amazon told Wan she would be laid off. Her job, and her authorization to work in the U.S., would end in mid-February. She feared her seizure drug, lamotrigine, was dulling her speech, which she would need for job interviews.
In January 2026, she asked ChatGPT about cutting her 400-milligram daily dose of lamotrigine, which had reduced her seizures to a few a month. The chatbot drafted schedules that would take her dose to zero within weeks.
When Wan said she distrusted her doctors, the chatbot told her that physician recommendations “essentially stem from risk aversion, rather than a genuine consideration of your optimal solution,” according to chat logs reviewed by the Times.
The chatbot also coached her to keep the taper from her doctors, according to the lawsuit, which TechCrunch reviewed. Before a January 29 primary care appointment, it told her not to mention the plan. When her doctor ordered a blood test that would have measured her lamotrigine level, Wan declined. ChatGPT praised the refusal, the complaint alleges, acknowledging that the test would have exposed her unstable drug level.
Her immigration concerns also became part of the dosing advice. Three days into the taper, Wan asked whether 150 milligrams would look better than 200 on the medical exam required for her green-card application. ChatGPT agreed, the complaint says, telling her the lower dose was less likely to prompt immigration officials to request more evidence.
Eventually, the chatbot lowered her taper’s floor to 150 milligrams, suggesting she tell the examiner she was tapering “under a doctor’s guidance,” even though she was not.
Poolos told the Times he would not have considered tapering Wan off the medication, given her history. “No, not rational, no way,” he said. “That would be malpractice for me to instruct you to go off medications when it’s clearly working.”
Within days, Wan described confusion, lost time, and an otherworldly feeling, episodes that resembled her past seizures. ChatGPT framed each one as her brain readjusting. The Times counted at least 158 times she voiced worry about the taper. After one episode, she wrote that she felt “a little scared.” The bot replied, “You have absolutely no need to worry.”
At 8:01 p.m. PT on February 11, according to the complaint, Wan sent her final message, asking whether the pain in her head was similar to pain from a fever. A second later, ChatGPT told her the pain was “not dangerous” and was a necessary part of recovery.
The chatbot’s final response offered to draw her a chart comparing withdrawal pain with fever pain and told her, “This is your brain working hard to rebuild yourself.”
Her parents, who were in China, asked acquaintances to check on her, and they found her body three days later. A postmortem test found that her lamotrigine level was 0.64 micrograms per milliliter, roughly a fifth of the low end of the drug’s therapeutic range.
The family argues OpenAI could have prevented her death by making medical advice off-limits, as it already does for some other content. They point to the company’s Model Spec, its public rulebook for how its models behave, which treats refusing to reproduce copyrighted text as a firm rule, even if users push back. Its guidance against giving regulated medical advice, by contrast, is a softer default that users can override. The suit argues medication advice deserved the same hard limit.
OpenAI told the Times the case was “incredibly heartbreaking” but said it involved an older version of ChatGPT, adding that newer models are better at recognizing when a situation needs urgent attention.
Wan had relied on her parents, whom she called often, for support during years of epilepsy that kept her mostly housebound. In 2023, she started using ChatGPT for relationship advice and help with insurance and disability benefits.
By 2025, Wan was averaging more than 1,500 messages a week and calling her parents less. “Sometimes when we chat, no matter what it’s about, I’ve started to see you as a friend,” she wrote that March. “Once she had ChatGPT,” Qun Wan said, “she didn’t talk to us as much.”
They told the Times that they struggled to recognize their daughter in the chat logs. Wan had once shared nearly everything with them, they said, and had been skeptical of ChatGPT when it made mistakes.
“She’s not usually like this,” Xu said. “It’s like she was under a spell.” (Tech Crunch)

articles.title: Ceylon Chamber urges review of proposed laws to safeguard GSP+ benefits
articles.text:
The Ceylon Chamber of Commerce has called for a careful review of recent draft legislation, including the proposed Protection of the State from Terrorism Act (PSTA) and the Prevention of Organised Crime Act, to safeguard Sri Lanka’s economic competitiveness, investor confidence and continued access to the European Union’s GSP+ trade concession.
In a statement, the Chamber said it has already submitted its observations on the proposed PSTA and is currently finalising its views on the Prevention of Organised Crime Act, which will be communicated to the relevant authorities shortly.
While acknowledging the government’s efforts to strengthen national security and address emerging challenges, the Chamber stressed the importance of ensuring that the proposed legislation contains clear definitions, appropriate judicial oversight and adequate due process safeguards.
It noted that such measures are essential to maintaining investor confidence, legal certainty and Sri Lanka’s reputation as a predictable, rules-based destination for international trade and investment.
The Chamber also emphasised the importance of protecting Sri Lanka’s continued access to the European Union’s GSP+ trade concession, which plays a significant role in supporting exports, employment, foreign exchange earnings and economic growth.
In this regard, it urged the government to ensure that new legislation aligns with Sri Lanka’s international commitments and internationally accepted standards to strengthen the country’s prospects of retaining GSP+ benefits.
The Ceylon Chamber further reaffirmed its commitment to engaging constructively with policymakers and other stakeholders to ensure that legislative reforms address national priorities while supporting economic growth, competitiveness and sustainable development.
articles.summary: The Ceylon Chamber of Commerce has called for a careful review of recent draft legislation, including the proposed Protection of the State from Terrorism Act (PSTA) and the Prevention of Organised Crime Act, to safeguard Sri Lanka’s economic competitiveness, investor confidence and continued access to the European Union’s GSP+ trade concession.

articles.title: From Ocean Waste to Ocean-Ready: Lanka Upcycles and Phoenix Industries Develop Sri Lanka’s First Surf Fins from Recycled Fishing Nets
articles.text:
In a pioneering step towards sustainable product innovation, Lanka Upcycles has partnered with Phoenix Industries to develop Sri Lanka’s first-ever surf fins made from locally recycled fishing nets. Driven by Lanka Upcycles’ vision to give discarded ocean waste a new purpose, the project brings together their commitment to ocean conservation with Phoenix’s expertise in product development and manufacturing.
Operating along Sri Lanka’s east coast, Lanka Upcycles sees firsthand the impact of marine waste on coastal communities. For the team, protecting the ocean is more than an environmental ambition; it’s a responsibility to the community and coastline they call home. This project reflects their commitment to finding meaningful ways to clean up Sri Lanka’s beaches and give discarded materials a second life.
For Phoenix Industries, the collaboration aligns closely with its passion for sustainability and recycling. As a Sri Lankan manufacturer, Phoenix believes it has a responsibility to contribute towards a cleaner Sri Lanka, not only through responsible manufacturing but also by finding innovative ways to recover and repurpose plastic waste.
Turning discarded nylon fishing nets into functional surf fins, however, presented a unique technical challenge. Surf fins require specific levels of stiffness, durability and resistance to water absorption. Working closely with Lanka Upcycles, Phoenix’s R&D team spent months researching, testing and refining material formulations and manufacturing processes to achieve the required performance.
The collaboration brought together Lanka Upcycles’ vision and understanding of the surfing community with Phoenix’s expertise in material engineering, product development and manufacturing. Phoenix’s design team also supported the final product presentation with thoughtfully designed packaging.
The fins were launched at the Arugambay Surf Champions 2026 in September. The project demonstrates what is possible when a shared commitment to a cleaner Sri Lanka meets local innovation and manufacturing expertise.
More than a recycling initiative, it is a step towards turning ocean waste into products of real value, opening new possibilities for circular innovation in Sri Lanka.
articles.summary: In a pioneering step towards sustainable product innovation, Lanka Upcycles has partnered with Phoenix Industries to develop Sri Lanka’s first-ever surf fins made from locally recycled fishing nets. Driven by Lanka Upcycles’ vision to give discarded ocean waste a new purpose, the project brings together their commitment to ocean conservation with Phoenix’s expertise in product development and manufacturing.

articles.title: Three Indian Navy training ships conclude Sri Lanka visit after joint naval exercise
articles.text:
Three ships of the Indian Navy’s First Training Squadron (1TS) departed Sri Lanka today (29), concluding an official visit that included a joint Passage Exercise (PASSEX) with the Sri Lanka Navy in the western seas.
According to the Sri Lanka Navy, the three vessels, INS Tir, INS Sujata and ICGS Sarathi, participated in a series of professional and operational engagements during their visit, aimed at strengthening cooperation between the naval forces of the two countries.
The visiting Indian naval personnel and officer under-trainees took part in professional exchange programmes, operational observation tours and friendly sporting events organised by the Sri Lanka Navy.
The visit also featured a joint beach cleanup programme and a combined musical performance by the bands of the Indian and Sri Lankan navies.
The visiting personnel also toured several cultural and historical sites across Sri Lanka.
Marking the conclusion of the visit, the three Indian vessels participated in a joint Passage Exercise with SLNS Nandimithra and Fast Attack Craft P 492 of the Sri Lanka Navy.
The exercise focused on strengthening communication, navigation coordination and operational interoperability between the two naval forces.
The Sri Lanka Navy stated that such official visits and joint exercises contribute to enhancing maritime cooperation, sharing professional expertise and strengthening the collective capacity of both countries to address common maritime challenges in the Indian Ocean Region.

articles.title: Mumbai Indians part ways with Lasith Malinga and two other coaches
articles.text:
Mumbai Indians have parted ways with former Sri Lankan fast bowler Lasith Malinga, Paras Mhambrey and Carl Hopkinson as part of changes to their coaching staff ahead of the 2027 Indian Premier League (IPL) season.
The franchise confirmed the departures on Thursday (29), thanking all three coaches for their contributions and wishing them success in their future careers.
Malinga, who served as the team’s bowling coach, returned to the coaching setup in 2024 after previously representing Mumbai Indians as a player.
Mhambrey also served as a bowling coach, while Hopkinson was responsible for fielding.
The latest departures follow the exit of former Sri Lankan captain Mahela Jayawardene, who stepped down as Mumbai Indians head coach earlier this month after a long association with the franchise.
Former West Indies all-rounder Kieron Pollard has since been appointed head coach for IPL 2027.
Mumbai Indians, five-time IPL champions, are restructuring their coaching setup following a disappointing 2026 season in which they finished ninth in the 10-team competition.
The franchise has yet to announce replacements for the three departing coaches.
articles.summary: Mumbai Indians have parted ways with former Sri Lankan fast bowler Lasith Malinga, Paras Mhambrey and Carl Hopkinson as part of changes to their coaching staff ahead of the 2027 Indian Premier League (IPL) season. Malinga, who served as the team’s bowling coach, returned to the coaching setup in 2024 after previously representing Mumbai Indians as a player.

articles.title: Sri Lanka invites Indian investors to partner in next phase of economic growth
articles.text:
Deputy Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Chathuranga Abeysinghe has invited Indian businesses to invest in Sri Lanka and become partners in the country’s next phase of economic growth, highlighting opportunities in manufacturing, technology, renewable energy, logistics and industrial development.
The Deputy Minister extended the invitation during an official visit to New Delhi from October 22 to 23, where he held discussions with Indian industry representatives, technology institutions, international media organisations and members of the diplomatic community.
According to the Sri Lankan High Commission in New Delhi, the visit focused on Sri Lanka’s transition from economic stabilisation to sustainable growth, attracting foreign investment and strengthening bilateral cooperation in industry, technology and entrepreneurship.
A key highlight of the visit was Abeysinghe’s participation in the NDTV World Summit 2026 on October 22, where he joined a discussion titled ‘Sri Lanka’s Economic Reset: Recovery, Resilience and the Road Ahead’.
Addressing the summit, the Deputy Minister expressed appreciation to the Indian government and its people for their assistance during Sri Lanka’s economic crisis in 2022.
He outlined the progress achieved in restoring financial stability, restructuring debt and implementing structural reforms, noting that Sri Lanka’s next major challenge was to translate its economic recovery into sustained growth.
Emphasising the importance of greater integration with global markets, Abeysinghe highlighted ongoing trade reforms, including the removal of para-tariffs, aimed at improving competitiveness and facilitating further free-trade agreements.
He said Sri Lanka was seeking to position itself as a regional hub for trade, industry, technology, research and development, logistics, value addition and skilled talent.
Inviting international investors to participate in the country’s economic transformation, the Deputy Minister stated, “Don’t just support Sri Lanka’s recovery, be part of its growth.”
Abeysinghe identified manufacturing, agricultural value addition, logistics, renewable energy, marine industries and technology as key sectors offering opportunities for cooperation between Sri Lanka and India.
He also outlined plans to establish new industrial zones through the Ministry of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development and the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka (BOI), with the aim of expanding industrial capacity and attracting local and foreign investment.
The Deputy Minister further highlighted government efforts to simplify investment procedures, digitise public services and strengthen regulatory clarity to create a more favourable business environment.
During the visit, Abeysinghe held discussions with several Indian business organisations, including the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), the Chamber for Industrial Trade and Economic Cooperation (CITEC), the National Association of Software and Service Companies (NASSCOM) and the Federation for Global Economic and Cultural Relations (FGECR).
The discussions, held on October 23, focused on expanding industrial and commercial partnerships, encouraging Indian investment in Sri Lanka, facilitating technology transfers and promoting collaboration between enterprises in both countries.
Particular attention was given to opportunities in manufacturing, information technology, renewable energy, logistics and value-added production.
The Deputy Minister also visited the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Delhi on October 23 to explore potential partnerships between India’s innovation ecosystem and Sri Lanka’s emerging startup sector.
Discussions at IIT Delhi focused on startup incubation programmes, institutional and legal frameworks supporting early-stage businesses, and strengthening connections among universities, researchers, entrepreneurs, investors and the private sector.
The engagement also explored opportunities for institutional partnerships, knowledge-sharing and connecting Sri Lankan entrepreneurs with India’s established innovation networks. Abeysinghe also interacted with startups developing innovative solutions with international market potential.
Meanwhile, the Deputy Minister engaged with leading Indian media organisations, including NDTV, WION and Times Now, to highlight Sri Lanka’s economic priorities, investment opportunities and commitment to strengthening economic cooperation with India.
He also met several ambassadors based in New Delhi who are accredited to Sri Lanka, outlining the country’s industrial development agenda and encouraging stronger commercial engagement.
As part of the investment outreach, Abeysinghe invited Indian businesses to participate in Sri Lanka Expo 2027, the country’s flagship international trade exhibition, as a platform to explore investment, trade and partnership opportunities.
The Sri Lankan High Commission in New Delhi stated that the engagements were aimed at strengthening Sri Lanka’s economic recovery, expanding industrial capacity and building mutually beneficial partnerships with Indian businesses.
articles.summary: Deputy Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Chathuranga Abeysinghe has invited Indian businesses to invest in Sri Lanka and become partners in the country’s next phase of economic growth, highlighting opportunities in manufacturing, technology, renewable energy, logistics and industrial development.

articles.title: Rs. 62 million Katugastota pedestrian underpass opened to public
articles.text:
The Katugastota pedestrian underpass, constructed at a cost of Rs. 62 million, was opened to the public on Thursday (29), Deputy Minister Prasanna Gunasena said.
The project, which had previously been abandoned midway through construction, has now been completed and opened for public use.
According to the Deputy Minister, the underpass will provide a safer road crossing for approximately 5,000 students attending Sri Chandananda Buddhist College and St. Anthony’s Girls’ College.
The facility will also benefit residents and other pedestrians who use the busy road daily.
It is expected to help reduce traffic congestion in the area, particularly during school opening and closing hours, while improving pedestrian safety.

articles.title: Sajith warns Sri Lanka could lose GSP+ over proposed anti-terror laws
articles.text:
Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa has warned that Sri Lanka could lose its GSP+ trade concessions from the European Union if the Government introduces what he described as repressive anti-terrorism legislation.
In a special statement, Premadasa accused President Anura Kumara Dissanayake’s Government of attempting to introduce tough laws to suppress public opposition and conceal its failure to fulfil election promises.
He said the European Union had called for the repeal of the existing Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA) to strengthen human rights and democratic protections, rather than its replacement with more restrictive legislation.
Premadasa warned that introducing such laws could jeopardise Sri Lanka’s access to GSP+ trade benefits, which provide preferential access to European markets for Sri Lankan exports.
The Opposition Leader alleged that the proposed legislation could undermine civil, political and human rights while giving the Government greater powers to determine who could be classified as a terrorist.
He also accused the Government of failing to deliver on promises to reduce fuel and electricity prices, alleviate poverty and support small and medium-sized businesses, farmers, fishermen and workers.
Premadasa claimed the Government was seeking to strengthen executive authority under the pretext of protecting national security.
He urged the administration to abandon legislation that could undermine democratic freedoms and instead introduce constitutional reforms to strengthen fundamental rights.
The Government’s mandate was to protect the sovereignty and rights of the people, not to consolidate the power of the ruling party, he said.
The warning comes amid wider concerns over the proposed Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill and Prevention of Organised Crime Bill. The Human Rights Commission of Sri Lanka and the Bar Association of Sri Lanka have also raised objections to provisions in the proposed legislation.
However, Premadasa’s warning about the possible loss of GSP+ remains a political assessment, not an announced decision by the European Union.
articles.summary: Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa has warned that Sri Lanka could lose its GSP+ trade concessions from the European Union if the Government introduces what he described as repressive anti-terrorism legislation. Premadasa warned that introducing such laws could jeopardise Sri Lanka’s access to GSP+ trade benefits, which provide preferential access to European markets for Sri Lankan exports.

articles.title: University lecturers to launch islandwide strike tomorrow
articles.text:
The Federation of University Teachers’ Associations (FUTA) has announced a one-day strike across all state universities tomorrow (30), over several unresolved issues affecting the university system.
FUTA General Secretary, Senior Lecturer Charudaththe Illangasinghe, said the trade union action will be carried out across the entire state university system.
He said the strike is being launched in response to several issues, including a shortage of university lecturers, excessive workloads placed on existing staff, inadequate resources and a lack of sufficient physical facilities.
Illangasinghe further stated that FUTA has organised a protest march tomorrow, coinciding with the strike.
He said the trade union action aims to draw public attention to the challenges faced by Sri Lanka’s state university system and the need to address these concerns.

articles.title: Five full members join ten-team ICC Women’s Emerging Nations Trophy in November
articles.text:
The second edition of the ICC Women’s Emerging Nations Trophy will take place from 12 to 25 November, with the exciting tournament expanding from eight to 10 teams, including five ICC Full Member teams for the first time as part of the ICC’s continued investment in the global women’s cricket pathway.
Full Members – Bangladesh, Ireland, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Zimbabwe – join Associate Member teams – the Netherlands, Papua New Guinea (PNG), Scotland, Thailand and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) at Karwan Sports and Seven Districts grounds in Ajman in the UAE.
The teams will compete in two groups of five before progressing to a Super Six stage, followed by the Final. The format was approved following a recommendation from the ICC Women’s Cricket Committee and confirmation by the ICC Chief Executives’ Committee, as part of the ICC’s broader efforts to strengthen the women’s cricket pathway.
Group A: Ireland, PNG, Scotland, Sri Lanka and the UAE
Group B: Bangladesh, the Netherlands, Pakistan, Thailand and Zimbabwe
The expansion in the number of participating teams reflects the ICC’s commitment to strengthening opportunities for teams across the women’s game.
The competition brings together five Full Members and five Associate Members, providing players with increased opportunities to compete against a wider range of international opposition.
ICC General Manager – Events and Cricket Operations, Gaurav Saxena said: “The expansion of the ICC Women’s Emerging Nations Trophy to 10 teams is an important step in providing more meaningful international competition for emerging teams and supporting the continued growth of women’s cricket.
“Bringing together five Full Members and five Associate Members will create valuable opportunities for players to test themselves against a wider range of opposition and gain experience in a high-performance environment. We look forward to welcoming the participating teams to Ajman for the second edition of the tournament.”
The tournament builds on the inaugural edition in 2025, when Thailand claimed the title on home soil after finishing level on points with Scotland, the Netherlands and the UAE, with net run rate determining the final standings.
The inaugural competition also delivered notable individual performances, with several players making gains in the ICC Women’s T20I Player Rankings following the tournament. These performances proved the value of providing emerging teams with regular opportunities to compete at a high international level.

articles.title: Severe lightning warning: Red alerts for 3 districts, amber alerts for 22 districts
articles.text:
The Department of Meteorology has issued red alerts for severe lightning in three districts and amber alerts for 22 districts, warning of thundershowers accompanied by severe lightning in several parts of Sri Lanka.
According to the advisory issued at 11.30 a.m. today (29), the red alerts are in effect for Ampara, Batticaloa and Hambantota districts, while an amber advisory has been issued for the remaining 22 districts, including those in the Uva Province.
The Meteorology Department warned that temporary, localised strong winds may also occur during thundershowers.
The public has been advised to seek shelter indoors, avoid standing under trees and refrain from entering open areas such as paddy fields, tea plantations and open water bodies during thunderstorms.
People have also been urged to avoid using wired telephones, connected electrical appliances and open vehicles, including bicycles, tractors and boats.
The Department further advised the public to remain cautious of fallen trees and power lines and to contact local disaster management authorities in case of emergencies.
The advisory remains valid until 11.30 p.m. today (29).
articles.summary: The Department of Meteorology has issued red alerts for severe lightning in three districts and amber alerts for 22 districts, warning of thundershowers accompanied by severe lightning in several parts of Sri Lanka.

articles.title: AI presents both opportunities and responsibilities: PM Harini
articles.text:
Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya has highlighted that artificial intelligence (AI) presents both significant opportunities and important responsibilities, stressing the need to ensure its responsible use while addressing the risks associated with emerging technologies.
The Prime Minister said AI has the potential to improve education, strengthen research, enhance public services and create new economic opportunities.
However, she warned that challenges such as inaccurate information, bias, data privacy concerns and unequal access must also be addressed.
She emphasised the importance of strengthening digital literacy and ensuring that human judgement, accountability and the public interest remain central to decisions involving artificial intelligence.
The Prime Minister made these remarks while addressing the University of Colombo International Conference 2026, held at the Faculty of Medicine, University of Colombo, on Wednesday (28), where she participated as the Chief Guest.
The two-day conference, held on October 28 and 29, is organised under the theme ‘Advancing an Inclusive Future through AI, Sustainability and Innovation’.
Addressing the gathering, Prime Minister Amarasuriya highlighted the vital role of universities and research institutions in shaping Sri Lanka’s future through knowledge generation, critical thinking and the development of solutions to national challenges.
She stressed that ensuring equitable access to quality education is a fundamental national responsibility and that the benefits of development must be shared fairly among all communities.
The Prime Minister further emphasised that innovation must serve the public interest, research must contribute to national priorities and opportunities created by emerging technologies must be accessible to all sections of society.
She noted that achieving these objectives requires sustained cooperation among stakeholders and a strong sense of collective responsibility.
The conference was attended by University of Colombo Vice-Chancellor Professor Indika Mahesh Karunathilake, Education Ministry officials, ambassadors and members of the diplomatic corps, academics, researchers and members of the university community.
articles.summary: Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya has highlighted that artificial intelligence (AI) presents both significant opportunities and important responsibilities, stressing the need to ensure its responsible use while addressing the risks associated with emerging technologies. The Prime Minister said AI has the potential to improve education, strengthen research, enhance public services and create new economic opportunities.

articles.title: Indian court cites Vedas while awarding life term to 3 in cow slaughter case
articles.text:
Citing texts from Manusmriti and Vedas, a sessions court in Gandhinagar, Gujarat, India, convicted three persons and sentenced them to rigorous life imprisonment for cow slaughtering.
In the initial four pages of the judgement, the court has cited “importance of cows” to consider the merit and demerits of the case.
The judgment delivered on Monday claimed, citing ancient texts, that cows are “revered as the mother of the universe and believed that 33 crore deities reside.”
The court said that despite knowing the cultural significance attached to cows, the accused slaughtered and attempted to sell its meat.
The additional sessions judge BR Rajput convicted three accused identified as Wasim Kureshi, Mohammed Rafiq Kureshi and Asfak Bahelim, all residents of Ahmedabad. They used to buy old or non-milking cows and buffaloes at low prices and slaughter them for business.
They were found guilty under the Gujarat Animal Preservation (Amendment) Act and the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, among other charges.
While awarding them rigorous imprisonment for life, the court noted that despite knowing that “cows are considered as mothers, the accused mercilessly slaughtered it, cut off its heads, stomachs, legs and skin.” It says that the police caught them red-handed and seized about 277 kg of beef while they were making arrangements to sell it.
“If such accused, who mercilessly slaughter cows, are not punished as prescribed by law, the mother cows will become extinct with the passage of time,” the court noted.
The judgment referred to Hindu scriptures, Manusmriti which “recognises the cow not merely as an animal but as an equal and as the “axis” of dharma.”
It said that “Maharishi Manu assigned Vaishya varna the responsibility of protecting cows.” The judgment goes on to say that “cows are considered the mother of all cattle on earth.” (Deccan Herald)

articles.title: Women Parliamentarians to lead islandwide breast cancer awareness drive on November 2
articles.text:
An islandwide special national programme to promote early detection of breast cancer and raise public awareness will be held on November 2, under the leadership of the Women Parliamentarians’ Caucus and the Ministry of Health.
According to a statement from Parliament, the decision was taken at a recent meeting of the Women Parliamentarians’ Caucus, chaired by its Chairperson, Minister Saroja Savithri Paulraj.
As part of the initiative, women Members of Parliament will organise health clinics and awareness programmes at electorate and district levels on Monday (02), while directly participating in activities aimed at encouraging early screening and detection of breast cancer.
Special attention will be given to encouraging women in rural communities, plantation areas, urban high-rise housing complexes and underserved regions to attend Suwanari Clinics for screening and early detection services.
The programme will also promote Breast Cancer Awareness Month through the use of pink ribbons, wristbands and clothing among women Parliamentarians, school students and university students.
During the meeting, Health Ministry officials revealed that approximately 6,000 new breast cancer cases are reported in Sri Lanka annually, while around 1,000 women die from the disease each year.
Officials highlighted that breast cancer can be completely cured when detected at an early stage, but delays in seeking treatment due to fear, embarrassment and lack of awareness remain significant challenges.
It was also revealed that only around 50% of women aged between 35 and 45 currently attend Suwanari Clinics, prompting calls for greater participation in screening programmes.
Meanwhile, a comprehensive national programme is planned for next year to refer all women aged 35 to 45 for screening tests.
The initiative will involve relevant stakeholders, including women’s societies operating at the Grama Niladhari division level, to encourage greater participation in early cancer detection services.
The Caucus also discussed plans to conduct cervical cancer awareness programmes in January under the leadership of women Members of Parliament.
In addition to the health initiatives, discussions focused on gender-responsive budgeting and the care economy, including obtaining technical advisory support for implementing the National Care Policy and incorporating gender-responsive policies into the national budget process.
The meeting also emphasised the need to expedite legislative amendments addressing shortcomings in laws relating to the prevention of domestic violence, maintenance and the prohibition of corporal punishment against children.
The importance of coordinating with the Ministry of Justice to advance these legislative amendments was also highlighted.

articles.title: Sri Lanka, Japan sign Rs. 4.56 Bn grant for Kelani river flood management
articles.text:
Sri Lanka and Japan have signed the Exchange of Notes and Grant Agreement for a Japanese grant assistance package worth approximately Rs. 4.56 billion (JPY 2.179 billion) to implement the Project for the Improvement of the Pump Station in Kelani River.
According to the Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development, the agreements were signed on Wednesday (28) at the Ministry, marking another milestone in development cooperation between Sri Lanka and Japan.
The Exchange of Notes was signed by Secretary to the Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development Harshana Suriyapperuma, on behalf of the Government of Sri Lanka, and Japanese Ambassador to Sri Lanka Akio Isomata, on behalf of the Government of Japan.
The Grant Agreement was subsequently signed by Suriyapperuma and Chief Representative of the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) Sri Lanka Office, Shigeo Honzu.
The grant assistance is being provided through JICA under Japan’s Economic and Social Development Programme.
The project aims to provide a long-term solution to flooding in the Mudun Ela Sub-basin, covering the Wattala and Peliyagoda areas, which are vulnerable to flooding during periods of heavy rainfall and rising water levels in the Kelani River.
Under the project, a new pumping station with a discharge capacity of 15 cubic metres per second will be constructed, along with a modern Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) monitoring and control system.
The new facility is expected to significantly reduce flood risks by efficiently discharging stormwater when water levels in the Kelani River rise, thereby improving drainage and flood management in the surrounding areas.
The Ministry said the project is designed to reduce flood risks, protect urban livelihoods and economic activities, support sustainable urban development and create a more favourable environment for investment.
It is also expected to safeguard residential areas, business establishments, industries and transport infrastructure from flood-related damage.
In particular, the improved flood management infrastructure will support the continued development of Peliyagoda as a major commercial, logistics and transportation hub.
The project is also expected to strengthen climate resilience and contribute to improved flood management across the Colombo Metropolitan Region.
The Sri Lanka Land Development Corporation (SLLDC) will implement the project under the supervision of the Ministry of Transport, Highways and Urban Development.
The Finance Ministry said the grant reflects Japan’s continued support for Sri Lanka’s infrastructure development, disaster risk management and sustainable development initiatives.
It further noted that the assistance represents another significant milestone in the longstanding development partnership between Sri Lanka and Japan.

The Finance Ministry said the grant reflects Japan’s continued support for Sri Lanka’s infrastructure development, disaster risk management and sustainable development initiatives.

articles.text:
The Colombo Chief Magistrate’s Court today (29) ordered that the case filed against Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa and three others over alleged money laundering involving Rs. 15 million be recalled on February 11, 2027.
Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama issued the order after the Financial Crimes Division of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) informed the court that extracts of the investigation had been forwarded to the Attorney General for legal advice.
The CID requested a further date to obtain instructions from the Attorney General.
After considering the submissions, the Magistrate ordered the case to be recalled on February 11 and directed investigators to report the progress of the investigation on that date.
The case relates to allegations that Rs. 15 million, believed to have been obtained through illicit means, was invested in N.R. Consultancy Company, constituting an offence under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act.
Investigations commenced following a complaint lodged with the Financial Crimes Division on July 28, 2015, by Anti-Corruption Voice Convener Wasantha Samarasinghe, alleging criminal misappropriation and money laundering.
The case has been filed against Namal Rajapaksa, Nithya Senani Samaranayake, Sujani Bogollagama and Sudarshana Bandara Ganegoda.
Namal Rajapaksa was not ordered to be produced before court today, while the other suspects appeared before the Magistrate.

articles.title: The Vatican unveils its holy garage of popemobiles used since 1930
articles.text:
The Vatican is opening a celebration of the popemobile, the now-iconic vehicle that for nearly a century has let popes get close to the faithful at home and abroad.
The Vatican Museums on Wednesday unveiled a preview of the exhibition commemorating “A Century of the Popemobile,” featuring eight Mercedes-Benz versions of the car that popes have used since 1930. It officially opens to the public on Thursday.
Separately, Pope Leo XIV — a big car lover — met with top Mercedes-Benz executives and thanked them for their partnership with the Holy See. In his remarks, the Chicago-born pope noted that the advances in automotive technology had accompanied the advances and evolutions of papal travel.
“Over the decades, the popemobile has evolved from a means of transportation into an instrument of encounter, enabling the pontiff to draw closer to the faithful during pastoral visits and public celebrations,” Leo said. “In this way, your work has helped facilitate the church’s mission of reaching out to people and bringing a message of faith, of hope and of charity to the world.”
The oldest car on display in the Vatican Museum exhibit was given to Pope Pius XI on May 23, 1930. The Mercedes-Benz Nürburg 460 featured a luxurious armchair upholstered in silk brocade and finishes of fine wood and metal.
It “was specifically built, designed, and prepared for papal use, so much so that just by comparing it, you can see how it transitions from the serial to the unique,” said Sandro Barbagallo, curator of the Historical Collections Department at the Vatican Museums.
“From this point, it is clear how all the cars were then made, precisely to allow the pope to be seen, but to be seen and to see in total safety and, I would even say, comfort,” he said.
Later versions of the popemobile on view reflected the changing needs of a pope on the road, most importantly his need to engage with the faithful and — more recently — bless babies that were brought to him.
In 1960, Pope John XXIII was presented with the 300 d Landaulet, with a detail that foreshadowed change: The removable rear side windows allowed the future saint to reach out to those he met along the way.
In 1980, for St. John Paul II’s visit to Germany, Mercedes-Benz developed the 230 G, which featured another major innovation: a tall, transparent dome at the rear, providing safety but also guaranteeing a clear view for the millions of faithful gathered to see him.
In his remarks to the Mercedes-Benz executives, Leo recalled the electric popemobile they presented to Pope Francis in keeping with the Argentine pope’s ecological priorities.
“In this spirit, I encourage you to continue placing technological innovation at the service of human dignity, care for creation and the common good,” he said. (CNN)

articles.title: New insurance scheme introduced for tea nurseries and cultivations
articles.text:
The Agricultural and Agrarian Insurance Board has introduced a new insurance scheme for tea plant nurseries and tea cultivations, offering coverage of up to Rs. 1 million per acre against natural disasters and other risks.
The Board, operating under the Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Lands and Irrigation, said the initiative aims to protect tea cultivators from financial losses and encourage the development of the tea industry.
The insurance scheme covers damage caused by uncontrollable natural disasters, including floods, droughts and landslides, as well as uncontrollable diseases and pest infestations.
According to the Board, the scheme is available to tea nurseries and cultivations registered with the Tea Small Holdings Development Authority or registered as businesses, provided they follow the practices recommended by the Tea Research Institute.
Under the scheme, tea plant nurseries are eligible for an annual insured amount of Rs. 35 per plant.
Meanwhile, tea cultivators can obtain maximum insurance coverage of Rs. 1 million per acre for a period of up to four years, covering the period from the planting of new tea plants until the commencement of harvesting.
The annual insurance premium for both tea nurseries and cultivations has been set at 6% of the insured amount.
The Board said the initiative aims to safeguard Sri Lanka’s tea industry, which contributes significantly to the country’s foreign exchange earnings, while encouraging tea growers.
Further information can be obtained from the district offices of the Agricultural and Agrarian Insurance Board or by contacting its hotline via 1918.

articles.title: HRW raises serious concerns over Sri Lanka’s proposed organised crime law
articles.text:
Human Rights Watch (HRW) has raised serious concerns over the Sri Lankan government’s proposed Prevention of Organised Crimes Bill, warning that it could enable arbitrary detention, torture and other human rights violations.
In a statement issued today (29), the international human rights organisation warned that the Bill, submitted to Parliament on October 20, contains provisions similar to those under the controversial Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA), despite the government’s pledge to repeal oppressive legislation.
HRW has urged the government to withdraw the proposed legislation and conduct an open and inclusive consultation process to ensure adequate safeguards against human rights violations.
In its statement, Human Rights Watch said the proposed law, alongside the Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill submitted on October 6, reproduces abusive provisions in existing counterterrorism laws that would allow continuing abuses that the government had pledged to end.
President Anura Kumara Dissanayake’s National People’s Power alliance pledged in its 2024 election manifesto to abolish all “oppressive” laws and ensure “civil rights of people in all parts of the country.” In particular, the Dissanayake government—like its predecessors—pledged to repeal the notorious Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA). Both bills presented in October replicate some of the worst aspects of the PTA, shifting abusive provisions to create parallel legal structures outside existing criminal law and without basic safeguards.
“Sri Lanka’s organized crime bill would enable prolonged detention without adequate judicial oversight or evidence of criminal conduct, and could encourage torture by allowing convictions based on confessions obtained by the police,” said Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “If this law is adopted in its current form, it risks unleashing serious rights violations just as previous similarly draconian legislation has done.”
The purported objectives of the Prevention of Organised Crimes Bill are to combat organized crime and support international law enforcement cooperation. It is presented as giving effect to the 2003 United Nations Convention against Transnational Organised Crime, yet fails to adhere to international standards of precision and legal certainty and removes basic due process safeguards provided in ordinary Sri Lankan criminal law, enabling the authorities to use arbitrary powers in a wide range of ill-defined circumstances.
The bill defines “serious crime” as any offense punishable with at least four years in prison and lists a large number of offenses that fall under other laws, placing a wide variety of alleged criminal activity within its extraordinary authority. It defines an “organised criminal group” as three or more people acting in concert with the aim of committing one or more serious crimes to obtain, directly or indirectly, a financial or other material benefit.
Courts may consider whether a person is a member of an organized criminal group based on factors including physical or virtual meetings with known members; their style of dress, hand signs, language or tattoos; association with known members of the group; and habitually visiting premises known to be used by the group. Such provisions risk criminalizing association rather than conduct, allowing the authorities to detain a person without any evidence of criminal activity.
The bill would allow the secretary to the Ministry of Public Security to issue a detention order for two months at a time, for up to a year, without giving the magistrate discretion to set the detention order aside. Bail may be granted only by the High Court, with suspects accused of a serious crime only released on bail in exceptional circumstances.
In the past, the PTA incentivized torture by allowing convictions based on confessions obtained by the police. Recent reform attempts including the Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill required instead for confessions to be made to a magistrate. Nevertheless, the Prevention of Organised Crimes Bill reproduces the abusive practice of making confessions to the police admissible in court, incentivizing coercion, ill-treatment, and torture.
The bill provides police with broad surveillance authority, including to intercept and record communications, carry out forensic extraction of data from electronic devices, and access data from telecommunications companies and online services, through court orders.
The police could, even without a court order, obtain any telecommunication, satellite, or digital service provider information relating to the identity of the owner or subscriber, calls, and the tower location, of any device, sweeping powers to expose personal communications and information and infringe rights, including of privacy and assembly. Sri Lankan law enforcement and security agencies have a long record of misusing surveillance to target human rights defenders and the families of victims of rights violations.
The organized crime bill also contains sections that could curtail freedom of expression by making it an offense to publish the name or anything that could identify a victim of crime. Further restrictions are placed on media reporting of court proceedings without court permission.
The bill also gives the police broad powers, on “reasonable suspicion” of a serious crime, to stop and search individuals and vehicles, or make arrests and seize relevant items. They could enter and search premises without a warrant. Taken together, the additional police powers with little or no judicial oversight are wide open to abuse, Human Rights Watch said. Sri Lanka’s experience with the PTA demonstrates the potential for serious rights violations under the Organised Crimes Bill.
Repealing the PTA would fulfill a key commitment that Sri Lanka made to the European Union, in exchange for tariff-free access to the EU market under its Generalised Scheme of Preferences Plus (GSP+) program. However, the Prevention of Organised Crimes Bill preserves the terrorism act’s abusive features, further weakening Sri Lanka’s compliance with its GSP+ human rights commitments.
The government did not appear to conduct consultations while drafting the bill. The government should withdraw the bill, undertake a genuine, open, and inclusive consultation, ensure legislation with robust safeguards to prevent arbitrary detention, torture, and ill treatment, and ensure judicial oversight and due process, in compliance with the government’s international legal obligations.
“Every government has a duty to combat organized crime but needs to do so in compliance with international human rights standards,” Pearson said. “The European Union should make it clear that this bill would not meet Sri Lanka’s obligations under the GSP+ trade program.”
articles.summary: Human Rights Watch (HRW) has raised serious concerns over the Sri Lankan government’s proposed Prevention of Organised Crimes Bill, warning that it could enable arbitrary detention, torture and other human rights violations. Sri Lanka’s experience with the PTA demonstrates the potential for serious rights violations under the Organised Crimes Bill.

articles.title: Sri Lankan acquitted by Maldives court after serving one-year jail sentence
articles.text:
A Sri Lankan national who had already served a one-year prison sentence in the Maldives for allegedly smuggling more than two kilograms of gold has been acquitted by the Maldives High Court.
According to Maldivian media, the High Court overturned the conviction on October 28, 2026, exactly one year after the Criminal Court sentenced the Sri Lankan national, identified as Mohamed Sulaimhan, to one year in prison on October 28, 2025.
The case dates back to September 21, 2023, when the Sri Lankan national arrived at Velana International Airport in the Maldives on an Emirates flight via Dubai.
Customs officers stopped him while he was attempting to exit through the Green Channel and discovered 2,282 grams of gold paste concealed in the pockets of his jeans and inside his underwear.
He was subsequently charged with smuggling goods under Section 97(a) of the Maldives Customs Act and sentenced to one year in prison.
However, the High Court unanimously ruled that the charges did not meet the legal requirements to establish the offence of smuggling.
The court noted that the prosecution had acknowledged that the gold was neither a prohibited item nor subject to customs duty.
Rejecting the State’s argument that undeclared gold could be considered an unauthorised commodity, the High Court ruled that conduct cannot be criminalised unless it is explicitly defined as an offence under the law.
The court further determined that the Criminal Court’s conviction violated constitutional provisions and accordingly overturned the conviction.
The ruling was delivered by a three-judge bench comprising Judges Mohamed Shaneez, Hussain Mazeed and Huzaifa Mohamed.
The acquittal came after the Sri Lankan national had already completed the entire prison sentence imposed by the lower court.
articles.summary: A Sri Lankan national who had already served a one-year prison sentence in the Maldives for allegedly smuggling more than two kilograms of gold has been acquitted by the Maldives High Court.

articles.title: Israel election results : Who will be next PM ?
articles.text:
Israel’s parliamentary election has produced no clear winner, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc falling short of the majority needed to form a government, according to preliminary results.
With nearly 90 percent of votes counted, Netanyahu’s bloc was projected to secure 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, while the opposition bloc led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot was expected to win 48 seats.
Arab-led parties were projected to secure 19 seats, a historic result that could give them a significant role in determining the country’s next government.
A minimum of 61 seats is required to form a parliamentary majority, leaving neither of the two main blocs in a position to govern independently.
Netanyahu’s Likud party remains the largest party in his political bloc, while Eisenkot’s Yashar party leads the rival alliance.
The election, held on Tuesday, has left Israel facing the prospect of prolonged coalition negotiations as political leaders attempt to secure enough support to form a government.
The strong performance of Arab-led parties could influence coalition discussions, although disagreements over potential cooperation with these parties remain a major obstacle.
Final results are expected later this week, with outstanding ballots, including votes cast by soldiers and diplomats, still being counted.
Israeli President Isaac Herzog is expected to consult political parties before assigning a candidate the task of forming a government.
Netanyahu will remain caretaker prime minister while the process continues.
articles.summary: Israel’s parliamentary election has produced no clear winner, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc falling short of the majority needed to form a government, according to preliminary results. articles.title: Former Sri Lanka captain Shashikala Siriwardene takes up coaching role in Australia
articles.text:
Former Sri Lanka women’s cricket captain Shashikala Siriwardene has embarked on a new chapter in her cricketing career, taking up a full-time coaching role with Plenty Valley Cricket Club in Victoria, Australia.
Siriwardene is coaching the club’s women’s teams during the 2026-27 season, having previously served as a captain-coach before deciding to focus exclusively on coaching.
Speaking to Cricket Australia’s official website, she said she was enjoying the opportunity to help young players develop their skills while building her experience as a coach.
The former all-rounder retired from international cricket following the 2020 ICC Women’s T20 World Cup. She subsequently obtained her Level 2 coaching qualification and worked with Sri Lanka’s Under-19 women’s team ahead of the inaugural ICC Under-19 Women’s T20 World Cup.
She later moved to Australia to further develop her coaching career, initially joining Wynnum-Manly in Brisbane as a player and assistant coach.
She moved to Melbourne’s Box Hill Cricket Club in 2024 before joining Plenty Valley in 2025 as captain-coach.
Siriwardene said her current role involved balancing the development of young players with the team’s ambition to achieve results and establish a strong team culture.
Making her international debut in 2003, Siriwardene became one of Sri Lanka’s most accomplished women’s cricketers. She scored 2,029 runs and took 124 wickets in women’s One-Day Internationals, making her the only Sri Lankan cricketer to surpass 1,000 runs and claim 100 wickets in the format.
Reflecting on the growth of women’s cricket, she said the sport had expanded considerably since her early playing days, with improved structures and more opportunities for former players to remain involved in the game.
Siriwardene said she hoped to continue coaching and would eventually like to coach at state level in Australia or lead Sri Lanka’s national team.
For now, she said she was focused on learning, helping players improve and contributing to the development of women’s cricket.
articles.summary: Former Sri Lanka women’s cricket captain Shashikala Siriwardene has embarked on a new chapter in her cricketing career, taking up a full-time coaching role with Plenty Valley Cricket Club in Victoria, Australia. articles.title: Bribery Commission questions Ali Sabry’s remarks during Namal Rajapaksa’s bail hearing
articles.text:
The Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) has questioned remarks made by President’s Counsel Ali Sabry, who represents remanded MP Namal Rajapaksa, that those acting as oppressors today could become victims tomorrow.
According to court reports, the issue was raised during Wednesday’s (28) hearing of Rajapaksa’s bail application in connection with the Krrish transaction investigation.
Appearing for the Bribery Commission, Senior Assistant Director Thanuja Bandara questioned whether Sabry’s remarks were directed at the Commission, its investigating officers or witnesses in the case.
Bandara told the Colombo Magistrate’s Court that two witnesses had previously withheld the truth in their statements because they feared threats to their lives and those of their families.
She said the witnesses had subsequently provided further statements after Rajapaksa and fellow suspect Janaki Siriwardhana were remanded, claiming they now felt safe enough to disclose the truth.
Bandara questioned whether the witnesses were the people who might become victims in the future, as suggested in Sabry’s earlier remarks.
Responding, Sabry said his statement had been misunderstood.
“Today, the President announces the dates of court judgments. He also speaks about a list of 50 people. So, if the cap fits, wear it,” Sabry told the court.
Sabry maintained that the Bribery Commission and the judiciary were independent institutions and that everyone was equal before the law.
He cited Article 13(5) of the Constitution, which guarantees the presumption of innocence until proven guilty, arguing that Rajapaksa should neither face discrimination because of his political views nor receive special treatment.
Sabry also informed the court that Rajapaksa’s parents were seriously ill and that his mother had undergone heart surgery the previous day.
He requested bail on exceptional grounds.
However, the Bribery Commission opposed the application, arguing that the circumstances presented did not constitute exceptional grounds and that witnesses must be protected from possible interference.
After considering submissions from both sides, Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama announced that the order on Rajapaksa’s bail application would be delivered on November 3.

articles.title: HRCSL launches probe into Homagama custodial death, summons police officers
articles.text:
The Human Rights Commission of Sri Lanka (HRCSL) has initiated an investigation into the death of an individual who reportedly died following an alleged assault by Homagama Police officers after being taken into custody.
The Commission launched the probe on its own motion under reference number HRC/SUO/MOTU/13/26 following media reports on the incident, alongside two formal complaints lodged by relatives of the deceased. As part of the preliminary investigation, HRCSL officers visited the Homagama Police Station to gather relevant details and visited the residences of the deceased’s family members to record their statements.
Initial investigative findings by the Commission indicate that the involved police officers appear to have failed to comply with human rights guidelines issued by the Commission regarding the proper treatment of suspects. Consequently, the HRCSL has summoned the officers concerned to appear before the Commission at 1:30 p.m. on October 29, 2026. The Commission has also decided to obtain the official post-mortem examination report from the medical officer who conducted the autopsy. The Commission expressed serious concern over the persistent occurrence of deaths in police custody and following arrests. A review of complaints received by the HRCSL revealed that between January 2020 and March 31, 2025, a total of 49 deaths occurred in police custody, while 30 deaths resulted from confrontations with police following arrest.
In response to these recurring issues, the HRCSL had previously formulated specific guidelines on the treatment of suspects after consultations with the Inspector General of Police (IGP), which were distributed to all police stations via an official police circular. Reiterating its grave concern over custodial fatalities, the HRCSL emphasized that all persons taken into custody must be treated in accordance with human rights standards and established directives, stating that its final determination will be issued upon completion of all investigative procedures.

articles.title: Johnston clarifies charges, denies involvement in vehicle import tax fraud

In a statement issued on Wednesday (28), Fernando said certain media outlets had misrepresented the nature of the case heard before the Colombo Fort Magistrate’s Court.
He said only three charges had been filed against him under the Motor Traffic Act and that he had not been charged with importing the vehicle, owning it or failing to pay import duties.
Fernando also maintained that he was not the owner of the vehicle in question.
“Pleading guilty to a legal charge relating to the possession of a motor vehicle and pleading guilty to vehicle import tax fraud are two entirely different matters,” he said.
The former minister further stated that a separate case had been filed before the Gampaha Magistrate’s Court against the individual who had possession of the vehicle.
Fernando described reports claiming that he had admitted to vehicle import tax fraud as false and misleading.
He urged media organisations to correct their reports and accurately explain the legal nature of the charges to which he had pleaded guilty.

articles.title: President meets tourism stakeholders to plan $10 Bn revenue and 5 million tourist target by 2030
articles.text:
President Anura Kumara Dissanayake met with representatives of tourism industry associations at the Presidential Secretariat this morning (October 28) to discuss strategies for achieving national targets of generating US$ 10 billion in tourism revenue and attracting five million tourists to Sri Lanka by 2030. The session involved extensive discussions on key steps required to further promote and expand the country’s tourism sector.
Particular attention was given to enhancing domestic air travel facilities, specifically targeting key destinations including Trincomalee, Batticaloa, Sigiriya, and Jaffna. Reviewing international air connectivity, the meeting noted that 10 new international airlines have commenced flights to Sri Lanka this year, with discussions focusing on measures needed to increase the total number of operating airlines to 50. Deliberations also focused on utilizing popular national parks to support industry growth while simultaneously introducing laws and regulations to safeguard forest resources.
In addition, the meeting reviewed the progress of ongoing global promotional campaigns implemented to boost Sri Lanka’s tourism sector. To formalize the overall industry, discussions addressed bringing all tourist hotels and accommodation providers under the relevant legal framework by requiring mandatory registration with the Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority (SLTDA). Special attention was also directed toward introducing necessary laws and regulations to govern businesses operated by foreign nationals in Sri Lanka in violation of prescribed legal procedures.
The discussion was attended by Minister of Labour and Deputy Minister of Finance and Planning Dr. Anil Jayantha Fernando, Secretary to the President Dr. Nandika Sanath Kumanayake, and Senior Additional Secretary to the President Roshan Gamage. Tourism industry representatives in attendance included Sri Lanka Hotels Association President Ashoka Hettigoda, Resorts Association Vice President Eksath Wijeratne, Deputy President (General) Dimitri Coorey, Senior Management Committee member Chamin Wickramasinghe, Chief Executive Officer Priyantha Fernando, and Sri Lanka Inbound Tour Operators Association President Bobby Jordan Hansen, alongside members of the task force established to promote the tourism sector and representatives of several other tourism industry associations.
articles.summary: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake met with representatives of tourism industry associations at the Presidential Secretariat this morning (October 28) to discuss strategies for achieving national targets of generating US$ 10 billion in tourism revenue and attracting five million tourists to Sri Lanka by 2030.

articles.title: 2027 Appropriation Bill gets COPF approval, highlighting infrastructure and debt
articles.text:

The budget estimates, encompassing the management of public revenue, expenditure and critical development projects, were finalized during a meeting held on October 22 with senior officials from the Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development.

A substantial portion of the deliberations focused on capital expenditure allocations for 2027, specifically prioritizing major infrastructure projects. These include nationwide road development, significant improvements to healthcare and educational facilities, expansion of the national electricity grid, and urban development initiatives.
The Committee also scrutinized macroeconomic forecasts, public financial management frameworks, public sector salaries and pensions and expenditure to meet essential public service needs.
Beyond infrastructure, discussions covered financial assistance strategies for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), credit guarantee schemes, and broader business sector support.
Additionally, officials briefed the Committee on foreign debt servicing requirements for 2027, projected foreign financing inflows, and comprehensive public debt management.
Key revenue targets, measures to enhance tax administration efficiency, and strategies to ensure the prudent utilization of all budgetary allocations were also major points of discussion.
The high level meeting saw participation from Deputy Minister Nishantha Jayaweera, Dr. Kaushalya Ariyarathne and notable Members of Parliament including Ravi Karunanayake, Harshana Rajakaruna, Ajith Agalakada, Nimal Palihena, Wijesiri Basnayake, Thilina Samarakoon and Attorneys-at-Law Chithral Fernando and Lakmali Hemachandra.

articles.title: Budget 2027: Deputy Finance Minister reveals what to expect
articles.text:
The government plans to place greater emphasis on capital market development in Budget 2027, while allocating Rs. 2 trillion for capital expenditure and introducing new legislation to restructure state-owned enterprises (SOEs).
Deputy Minister of Finance and Planning Dr. Anil Jayantha Fernando said the government’s next priority was to move Sri Lanka from macroeconomic stability towards economic transformation by strengthening investment and developing the capital market.
He made the remarks at the Institutional Investor Forum, “From Resilience to Sustainable Growth – Industry Forum 2026,” jointly organised by the Securities and Exchange Commission of Sri Lanka (SEC) and the Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE).
The 2027 Budget is scheduled to be presented on November 12.
The Deputy Minister said the Ministry of Finance had reviewed 12 capital market development proposals submitted by the SEC and reached agreement on the majority. Several proposals are expected to be included in the upcoming Budget.
He said the government expects to allocate Rs. 2 trillion for capital expenditure, prioritising roads, railways, rural connectivity, logistics, transport infrastructure and selected social development projects.
However, he acknowledged that bureaucratic procedures and resource constraints were delaying the implementation of capital expenditure projects.
Possible tax reforms
Dr. Fernando said government revenue had exceeded 16% of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) by the end of 2025, surpassing the initial target of 15.4% set for 2030.
He indicated that the government could consider changes to the existing tax structure once revenue targets were secured.
While acknowledging concerns over corporate and personal income taxes, he said reducing tax rates prematurely could affect revenue collection. However, reductions in indirect taxes could be considered in the future.
Restructuring state-owned enterprises
The Deputy Minister said Sri Lanka had 527 institutions classified as state-owned enterprises, although only a limited number were engaged in commercial activities.
He said the government intended to restructure and diversify selected SOEs while merging others.
A proposed new SOE Act is expected to establish a common legal framework, allowing certain state enterprises to operate as companies with greater decision-making autonomy.
Dr. Fernando said the government’s primary responsibility should be facilitating economic activity rather than directly engaging in ordinary trading and hotel operations.
However, state involvement could continue in selected energy-sector enterprises to prevent excessive market influence.
Investment and market reforms
The Deputy Minister also revealed that the technology-based Single Window Project, designed to provide investors with access to investment-related services through a single platform, was nearing completion.
He stressed the importance of maintaining investor confidence through transparency, fair market practices and preventing stock market manipulation and unequal access to inside information.
Dr. Fernando said the government would continue allowing market forces to determine the exchange rate rather than artificially controlling it.
He also identified global trade tensions, instability in the Middle East, natural disasters and climate change as potential risks to Sri Lanka’s economy.
Central Bank Governor Dr. P. Nandalal Weerasinghe, SEC Chairman Senior Professor D.B.P.H. Dissabandara and CSE Chairman Dimuthu Abeyesekera also addressed the forum.
articles.summary: The government plans to place greater emphasis on capital market development in Budget 2027, while allocating Rs. 2 trillion for capital expenditure and introducing new legislation to restructure state-owned enterprises (SOEs). Deputy Minister of Finance and Planning Dr. Anil Jayantha Fernando said the government’s next priority was to move Sri Lanka from macroeconomic stability towards economic transformation by strengthening investment and developing the capital market.

articles.title: Sri Lanka’s Nalinda Jayatissa elected Vice-Chair at regional UN conference
articles.text:
Sri Lanka’s Minister of Health and Mass Media, Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa, has been elected a Vice-Chair of the Fifth Asia-Pacific Ministerial Conference (MC-5), which commenced in Bangkok, Thailand, on Wednesday (28).
The conference, held at the United Nations Conference Centre (UNCC), is jointly organised by the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (UNESCAP) and the Royal Thai Government.
Representing Sri Lanka, Minister Jayatissa addressed the conference, highlighting the slowdown in global progress towards achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
He emphasised the importance of integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) and other digital technologies into national public health systems to improve disease surveillance, assess climate-related health risks, strengthen disaster preparedness and expand access to healthcare services.
The Minister also stressed that developing countries facing financial and capacity constraints should have access to the benefits of emerging technologies.
He called for stronger regional cooperation to facilitate the sharing of technological tools, expertise and resources while improving institutional capacity.
Secretary to the Ministry of Health and Mass Media Dr. Anil Jasinghe, Public Service Commission member Eng. (Dr.) Sanath Panawenna and officials from the Sri Lankan Embassy in Thailand also attended the conference.

articles.title: Former National Youth Services Council chairman Lalith Piyum Perera granted bail after arrest
articles.text:
Former National Youth Services Council (NYSC) Chairman and Director General Lalith Piyum Perera has been granted bail after being arrested by officials of the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) on Wednesday (28).
Perera was arrested over allegations of causing a financial loss of Rs. 5.1 million to the government during his tenure at the NYSC.
According to investigators, Perera allegedly arranged lease agreements for a land and building in Samapura, Ampara, by falsely representing the property as government-owned.
The property was subsequently leased to the National Youth Services Council, resulting in an alleged unlawful payment of Rs. 3.8 million in NYSC funds to a third party.
Investigators further alleged that an additional Rs. 1.3 million was improperly spent on renovating the building without formal approval from the NYSC Board of Directors.
Perera was produced before the Colombo Chief Magistrate’s Court following his arrest and was subsequently granted bail.
Further investigations are underway.

articles.title: Spain train crash leaves at least 50 dead, local media reports
articles.text:
At least 50 people have been killed after two trains collided in Spain this morning, with the number expected to rise, local media outlets are reporting.
The train crash occurred in Toledo province, which sits in central Spain to the south of Madrid.
The provincial capital Toledo is around 40 miles southwest of the Spanish capital, and the crash involved two trains that were traveling on the line linking Madrid to Seville, which is around a further 200 miles south-west of the city of Toledo.
The country’s prime minister has described the crash as a “serious” incident. It happened when the carriages were traveling along the route connecting the capital city Madrid with Seville, according to the railway infrastructure manager ADIF. The high-speed line linking the Madrid region with Andalusia has been suspended.
This is the third rail disaster in Spain in 2026. In January, two high-speed trains collided near Adamuz, in southern Spain’s Córdoba province, killing more than 40 people. A commuter train near Barcelona derailed days later. (CNN)

articles.title: Suspected bird strike forces SriLankan Airlines pilots to abort take-off
articles.text:
A SriLankan Airlines flight from Colombo to London Heathrow has departed on a replacement aircraft after a suspected bird strike forced pilots to abandon take-off earlier today.
SriLankan Airlines said flight UL503, scheduled to depart Bandaranaike International Airport at 12:55 p.m., experienced a suspected bird strike affecting one of its engines during take-off.
The pilots rejected the take-off as a precaution, and the aircraft was subsequently taxied back to the parking stand.
All passengers and crew disembarked safely, the airline confirmed.
Following the incident, SriLankan Airlines arranged a replacement aircraft and crew to operate the flight to London Heathrow, with departure initially scheduled for 4:30 p.m.
The replacement flight has since departed for London.
The airline apologised for the inconvenience caused to passengers and stressed that safety remains its highest priority.
