articles.title: Sri Lanka and US discuss expanding trade, tourism and maritime security cooperation
articles.text:
Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya and US Ambassador to Sri Lanka Eric Meyer have held discussions on strengthening bilateral cooperation in trade, tourism, maritime security and education.
According to the Prime Minister’s Media Division, the discussions took place at Temple Trees on Tuesday (27), during a meeting between the Prime Minister and the US Ambassador, accompanied by a delegation.
Both sides explored opportunities to expand bilateral trade and economic relations, strengthen cooperation in the tourism sector and promote Sri Lanka as a destination for American tourists.
The discussions also focused on enhancing maritime security cooperation, including joint efforts to address shared maritime challenges.
During the meeting, PM Amarasuriya acknowledged the longstanding contribution of the Fulbright Scholarship Programme towards strengthening educational and academic cooperation between the two countries and stressed the importance of further expanding the programme.
Meanwhile, Ambassador Meyer briefed the Prime Minister on the US Peace Corps English language training programme and its potential contribution to improving English language education in Sri Lanka.
Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening the longstanding relationship between Sri Lanka and the United States through continued dialogue and cooperation in areas of mutual interest.
The meeting was also attended by US Embassy Deputy Chief of Mission David Myers, Secretary to the Prime Minister Pradeep Saputhanthri, Additional Secretary to the Prime Minister Sagarika Bogahawatta, and officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The discussions also focused on enhancing maritime security cooperation, including joint efforts to address shared maritime challenges.

articles.title: Cyclone Arnab weakens: Showers and strong winds forecast for several areas
articles.text:
The Department of Meteorology says the influence of Cyclone Arnab on Sri Lanka’s weather has gradually weakened after the storm crossed the coast of Andhra Pradesh, India.
In its general weather forecast for the next 36 hours, issued at 4.00 p.m. today (28), the Department said several spells of showers are expected in the Western and Sabaragamuwa provinces and in the Kandy, Nuwara Eliya, Galle and Matara districts.
Showers or thundershowers are also expected at a few places in the Uva Province and the Batticaloa and Ampara districts after 1.00 p.m. tomorrow (29).
Mainly fair weather conditions are forecast for other parts of the island.
Meanwhile, strong winds of around 30–40 kmph can be expected at times over the western slopes of the Central Hills, the Northern, North-central and North-western provinces, and the Trincomalee and Hambantota districts.
The Department has urged the public to take adequate precautions to minimise damage caused by temporary localised strong winds and lightning during thundershowers.

articles.title: Sajith warns Sri Lanka risks becoming a police state following death of youth in custody
articles.text:
Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa has questioned whether the death of a young man in police custody in Homagama is another step towards Sri Lanka becoming a police state.
In a special statement, Premadasa expressed serious concern over the death of Ishara Harshana, who died while in the custody of Homagama Police.
He said relatives who visited the police station on October 25 to inquire about Harshana had reportedly observed injuries on his body.
Premadasa called for an independent and transparent investigation into the death, stressing that police have a responsibility to ensure the safety and well-being of individuals in their custody.
He said the death raised serious concerns about constitutional protections and the responsibility of law enforcement authorities to safeguard human life.
The Opposition Leader also linked the incident to two proposed pieces of legislation aimed at combating organised crime and terrorism, warning that certain provisions could undermine fundamental rights and the rule of law.
He alleged that the proposed laws could restrict freedom of expression, political freedom and the right to peaceful assembly, potentially paving the way for authoritarian and one-party rule.
Premadasa said governments have a responsibility to strengthen democracy rather than restrict democratic freedoms.
He stressed that legislation aimed at protecting national security and combating organised crime must comply with international standards and human rights obligations.
The Opposition Leader called for justice for Ishara Harshana and urged the public to oppose any attempt to turn Sri Lanka into a police state.
He also pledged to provide political leadership to efforts aimed at preventing the introduction of laws that could undermine democratic rights and freedoms.
articles.summary: Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa has questioned whether the death of a young man in police custody in Homagama is another step towards Sri Lanka becoming a police state. In a special statement, Premadasa expressed serious concern over the death of Ishara Harshana, who died while in the custody of Homagama Police.
